name: Matred
title: Mother of Mehetabel, an Edomite woman
summary: Matred is a woman mentioned in the Bible's genealogies as the mother of Mehetabel, who was the wife of the Edomite king Hadar (also called Hadad). She is known exclusively through genealogical references concerning the kings of Edom, and her name appears in both Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the list of Edomite kings
keyEvents.description: Matred is mentioned as the daughter of Me-Sahab and the mother of Mehetabel in the genealogy of the kings of Edom, in connection with King Hadar's wife.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Matred's name is repeated in 1 Chronicles in a parallel genealogy of the kings and rulers of Edom.

keyEvents.title: The Kingdom of Edom
keyEvents.description: Through her daughter Mehetabel, Matred is linked to the line of Edomite kings, which descends from Esau. The kings of Edom ruled before Israel had its first king.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Descendants
keyEvents.description: Matar is part of the broader narrative about Esau's descendants and their establishment in the land of Edom, as described in Genesis 36.
